tasks.short: Log every reminder, call, promise to pay and dispute in the customer's AFAS dossier and the collections Excel.

today.trigger: After each call, email or letter to a customer with an overdue invoice.
steps: Open the debtor in AFAS Profit and check open items
Type a note about the call or email and any promise-to-pay date
Update the collections tracker in Excel (status, next action, owner)
Save relevant emails from Outlook to the dossier or SharePoint
drudgery: Retyping what was said on the phone
Keeping AFAS and the Excel tracker in sync
today.time_sinks: Double entry between AFAS and Excel, and notes written after the fact from memory.

lenses.faster: Emails and call notes are summarised into a fixed note format (contact, amount, promise date, dispute reason) and written to AFAS in one click; the Excel tracker goes away.
lenses.autonomous: Every outgoing reminder and incoming customer email is logged to the debtor automatically; a promise-to-pay date creates a follow-up task.
lenses.ambitious: A complete, searchable history per customer that the auditor, the Controller and sales can read without asking.
lenses.joy: No more retyping calls at the end of the day; the officer just checks the summary.
lenses.options: The summary can propose the next action (wait, call, escalate) with the reason.
lenses.altitude: The officer designs the note template and status codes and spot-checks the logging quality weekly.
reach: Sales account managers' view of customer payment behaviour

tasks.human_edge: Judging what a customer really meant on the phone and recording disputes fairly; notes can end up in court or with a credit insurer.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured emails and call notes go in, a structured note with fixed fields comes out inside a deterministic AFAS workflow.

in_practice.trigger: Email sent or received on a debtor with open items, or call ended.
steps: Match email or call to debtor and invoices in AFAS
LLM extracts contact, amounts, promise date, dispute reason
Write note and status to AFAS dossier via API
Create follow-up task on promise date
Flag low-confidence matches for the officer
in_practice.human_gate: Officer reviews flagged notes and any note that records a dispute or a payment arrangement.
data_needed: Call transcripts or short dictated notes

evidence.claim: Credit management tools for the Dutch market log dunning actions and customer contact per debtor and connect to AFAS.
Copilot in Outlook and Teams can summarise email threads and meetings.
Structured extraction of promise-to-pay dates from emails is reliable enough with a review queue.

risks: Wrong customer match puts notes on the wrong dossier
Recording calls needs consent and an AVG basis
Summaries that soften or harden what the customer said
research_questions: Does the AFAS Profit API allow writing dossier items with attachments for debtors?
What share of collection contacts is email vs phone today?
Will the works council and customers accept call transcription for summaries?

tasks.short: Run the aging list each morning, find who is late, and decide who to chase first.

today.trigger: Daily start of work and weekly DSO review.
steps: Export open items and aging from AFAS to Excel
Filter by days overdue and amount
Cross-check Power BI DSO dashboard and credit limits
Build a call and reminder list for the day
drudgery: Checking which items are already disputed or promised
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the same worklist every day and sorting out items that are already in dispute.

lenses.faster: A ranked worklist is ready at 08:00 with disputes and promises already filtered out.
lenses.autonomous: Rules flag customers who exceed credit limit, break a promise, or shift payment behaviour, without anyone running a report.
lenses.ambitious: Risk scoring on every customer, including early warnings from Graydon or Creditsafe and KvK, not only the top 20.
lenses.joy: No more Excel exports; the officer starts the day calling the right people.
lenses.options: Show two or three ways to sort the day (by cash at risk, by age, by promise broken).
lenses.altitude: The officer owns the scoring rules and thresholds and tunes them each month against what actually got paid.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which customers matter commercially and when a late payer is a real risk rather than a slow process.
tasks.pattern_why: Aging, limits and promise dates are structured data and the prioritisation rules can be written down.

steps: Compute aging, overdue amount and broken promises per debtor
Apply credit-limit and risk-score rules
Exclude disputed items and open payment plans
Publish ranked worklist to Power BI and Teams
in_practice.human_gate: Officer reviews the top of the list and adjusts priorities; rule changes approved by the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset with daily snapshot

evidence.claim: Collections worklists ranked by risk are standard in AR automation tools.
Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract can carry the aging and ranking logic.

risks: Stale data if the nightly extract fails
Rules that ignore strategic customers
External credit data costs and AVG for sole-trader customers
research_questions: How many debtors are overdue on a typical day, and how is the list prioritised now?
Does the nightly extract include promise and dispute fields?
Did past write-offs show warning signs that a rule would have caught?

tasks.short: Send reminders and demand letters and call customers who are late paying.

today.trigger: Invoice passes due date or a reminder stage.
steps: Run AFAS reminder batch and check the letters
Write individual emails to larger customers
Call key accounts and those past second reminder
Send final notice with statutory interest and collection costs
drudgery: Checking each reminder for disputes before sending
Looking up contact persons and invoice copies
today.time_sinks: Pre-checking batches and chasing the right contact at the customer's accounts payable.

lenses.faster: Reminder batches run with disputes excluded and invoice copies attached; personal emails come pre-drafted.
lenses.autonomous: First and second reminders go out on schedule; calls are planned only where the rules say so.
lenses.ambitious: Every overdue customer gets a timely, correct reminder, including small accounts that are now ignored.
lenses.joy: The officer spends time on calls that matter instead of checking letters.
lenses.options: Draft the same message in firm, neutral and relationship-first tone, in Dutch or English.
lenses.altitude: The officer designs the dunning sequence per customer segment and watches its effect on DSO.

tasks.human_edge: The phone call: reading the customer, keeping the relationship, deciding when to be firm.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps with exceptions (disputes, contacts, attachments); the final notice has legal weight and needs a person.

in_practice.trigger: Daily after the worklist is built.
steps: Select debtors per dunning stage and exclude disputes
Draft reminders with invoice copies and correct interest
Send stages 1-2 automatically
Queue final notices and call list for the officer
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves every final notice and any message to a key account.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit has a built-in reminder (aanmaning) process.
Dutch credit management tools automate multichannel dunning flows.

risks: Reminding a customer with a valid dispute damages the relationship
Wrong statutory interest or collection costs (art. 6:119a BW, WIK for small customers)
Tone mismatch with key accounts
research_questions: What share of reminders today goes to items that turn out to be disputed?
Which customers does sales insist on handling personally?
Does a faster stage-1 reminder measurably cut DSO here?

tasks.short: Answer customer emails and calls about invoices, credits, rates and disputed charges.

today.trigger: Customer email or call about an invoice.
steps: Find the invoice and order in AFAS
Ask operations for proof of delivery or rate agreement
Check contract or rate card on SharePoint
Reply, or arrange a credit note with the Bookkeeper
today.time_sinks: Waiting on operations and searching for the right contract version.

lenses.faster: Draft replies come with the invoice, order, rate agreement and proof of delivery already attached.
lenses.autonomous: Simple requests (invoice copy, statement, payment confirmation) are answered automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every dispute is classified by cause, so finance and operations can fix the recurring ones (wrong rates, missing surcharges).
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste of invoice PDFs; the officer handles the real disputes.
lenses.options: Propose credit, partial credit or uphold, with the evidence for each.
lenses.altitude: The officer maintains the answer library and dispute categories and reviews the monthly dispute report.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a complaint is fair and agreeing a credit with the customer.
tasks.pattern_why: It needs several lookups across systems and has exceptions; credits and dispute answers need approval.

in_practice.trigger: Email arrives in the collections mailbox.
steps: Classify request (copy, statement, dispute, payment query)
Fetch invoice, order and contract data
Auto-send simple answers
Draft dispute reply with evidence and suggested outcome
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves every dispute reply and every credit proposal.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor dossier and dispute log

evidence.claim: AR tools offer customer portals for invoice copies and dispute registration.
Email classification and draft replies for finance mailboxes work with a review step.

risks: Auto-replies with the wrong invoice or a confidential document
Proof of delivery lives outside the listed systems
Promising credits the company does not owe
research_questions: What share of customer questions are simple copy or statement requests?
Where is proof of delivery stored and can it be reached by API?
What are the top five dispute causes over the last year?

tasks.short: Convince late payers to pay, agree payment plans, and use our lien on stored goods if needed.

today.trigger: Customer past final notice or broken promise.
steps: Review account history and relationship with sales
Call the customer and negotiate amount and date
Agree a payment plan within the authority limits
Consider retention of goods in our warehouse with the Finance Director
Confirm the agreement in writing
drudgery: Preparing the account history before each call
today.time_sinks: Preparing calls and getting internal approval for plans and retention.

lenses.faster: A one-page call briefing (history, disputes, promises kept, credit score, stock we hold) is ready before each call.
lenses.autonomous: Payment plan confirmations and instalment reminders run on their own once agreed.
lenses.ambitious: Every larger debtor gets a prepared negotiation, not only the ones the officer has time for.
lenses.joy: Less preparation, more time in the conversation the officer is good at.
lenses.options: Three payment-plan scenarios with cash impact and risk, within the authority matrix.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets the negotiation playbook and authority limits with the Finance Director.
reach: Finance Director decisions on retention of goods

tasks.human_edge: Trust, persuasion and judgement in a live conversation; using retention rights on goods carries legal and commercial risk.
tasks.pattern_why: The person leads the negotiation; AI prepares, suggests options and drafts the follow-up.

in_practice.trigger: Debtor appears on the call list for negotiation.
steps: Assemble briefing from AFAS, emails and credit data
Suggest payment-plan options within limits
Officer calls and agrees terms
Draft confirmation and schedule instalments
in_practice.human_gate: Officer and, above limits, Finance Director decide terms and any retention of goods.

evidence.claim: LLM-generated call briefings and draft confirmations are routine copilot uses.
Collections platforms support payment plans with automatic instalment tracking.

risks: Over-reliance on suggested options in a tense call
Applying retention of goods wrongly (art. 3:290 BW, logistics terms)
Scripts that feel pushy to long-term customers
research_questions: How often is retention of goods used and with what outcome?
What share of payment plans is honoured in full?
Does a prepared briefing shorten calls or raise the amount collected?

tasks.short: Match incoming Rabobank payments to open invoices in AFAS and sort out the ones that don't match.

steps: Import camt.053 statement into AFAS
Let AFAS auto-match on invoice number
Work through unmatched lines using remittance emails
Post partial payments, deductions and overpayments
drudgery: Splitting lump-sum payments across many invoices
today.time_sinks: Collective payments without invoice numbers and short payments with no reason given.

lenses.faster: Remittance advices from email and PDFs are read and matched automatically; only true exceptions remain.
lenses.autonomous: Statements import and post on arrival; deductions are tagged as disputes and routed.
lenses.ambitious: Same-day cash position for FP&A and almost no unapplied cash at month end.
lenses.joy: No more puzzling over lump sums; the officer handles the odd ones.
lenses.options: For an unclear payment, propose the two or three most likely invoice combinations.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets match rules and tolerances and reviews the exception rate weekly.
reach: Month-close cash reconciliation for the Accountant

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do with short payments and unexplained deductions.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank lines and open items are structured; an LLM step only reads unstructured remittance advices.

steps: Import statement into AFAS
Rule-based matching on reference, amount and debtor
LLM reads remittance emails for unmatched lines
Post matches above confidence threshold
Queue the rest with suggested matches
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves suggested matches and all deductions.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS cash journal and match log

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit imports bank statements and matches payments automatically.
AI cash application reads remittances and matches payments to invoices.

risks: Wrong posting makes a paid customer look late
Overpayments not refunded on time
Tolerance rules that hide small systematic deductions
research_questions: What is the current auto-match rate in AFAS?
How do the largest customers send remittance information?
How much unapplied cash is there at month end?

tasks.short: Keep customer master data right: address and contact changes, bankruptcies, closed companies.

today.trigger: Customer letter, returned mail, or news of a bankruptcy.
steps: Check KvK for the change or status
Update address, contact or bank details in AFAS
Check the insolvency register for bankrupt customers
Block account and file the claim with the trustee
today.time_sinks: Finding out about changes after invoices bounce or a claim deadline is close.

lenses.faster: KvK and insolvency monitoring pushes changes as ready-to-approve updates.
lenses.autonomous: A bankruptcy publication blocks the account and starts the claim checklist the same day.
lenses.ambitious: Clean master data for all debtors, checked monthly, not only when something goes wrong.
lenses.joy: No more surprise bankruptcies discovered weeks late.
lenses.options: For a change, show what it affects (open orders, stock held, credit insurance).
lenses.altitude: The officer owns the master-data rules and the monitoring list.

tasks.human_edge: Changes to bank details are a fraud risk and need a call-back check.
tasks.pattern_why: KvK and insolvency data are structured feeds; updates follow fixed rules.

in_practice.trigger: KvK change or insolvency publication for a monitored customer.
steps: Match the event to the AFAS debtor
Prepare the master-data change
Block account for bankruptcy or suspension
Notify officer, sales and credit insurer task
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves every master-data change; bank detail changes need a call-back.

evidence.claim: KvK offers APIs and change monitoring for registered companies.
Credit data providers alert on insolvency and company changes.

risks: Payment fraud via fake bank-detail changes
Missing KvK numbers in AFAS break matching
AVG for sole traders' personal data
research_questions: How many debtors have a valid KvK number in AFAS?
How many bankruptcies were noticed late last year and what did it cost?
Does the credit insurer policy require notification within set days?

tasks.short: When customers ignore us: block credit, alert sales, notify insurer, hand the file to the collection agency or lawyer.

steps: Propose credit block to Finance Director and inform sales
Stop new shipments or hold goods
Notify credit insurer of overdue
Build the file (invoices, contract, correspondence) and send to agency or lawyer
drudgery: Writing the same handover email each time
today.time_sinks: Building the dossier and waiting on approvals.

lenses.faster: The handover dossier and insurer notice are assembled in minutes from AFAS and email.
lenses.autonomous: Escalation tasks open automatically when deadlines pass, including insurer notification dates.
lenses.ambitious: No missed insurer deadlines and consistent escalation across all three sites.
lenses.joy: The officer decides; the paperwork is done.
lenses.options: Compare agency, lawyer or settlement with expected recovery and cost.
lenses.altitude: The officer designs escalation rules and reviews recovery results per route.
reach: Legal handover normally done by the Finance Director

tasks.human_edge: Choosing to escalate a customer is a commercial and legal decision with sales.
tasks.pattern_why: Multi-step work across systems with exceptions; every block or handover needs approval.

in_practice.trigger: Final notice deadline passes without payment or reply.
steps: Propose credit block and notify sales in Teams
Prepare insurer overdue notification
Assemble dossier PDF from AFAS, SharePoint and emails
Draft handover to agency or lawyer
in_practice.human_gate: Officer and Finance Director approve block and handover.

evidence.claim: Dutch credit management tools hand over files to collection agencies through integrations.
Dossier assembly from email and ERP is a fit for an agent with review.

risks: Blocking a key account without sales alignment
Sharing personal data with third parties without AVG agreements
Missed insurer deadlines if rules are wrong
research_questions: How many files go to agencies or lawyers per year and with what recovery?
What are the credit insurer's notification terms?
Who has authority to stop shipments today?

role.altitude: From chasing invoices to running the receivables system: owning the dunning rules, match rules, risk scores and escalation playbook, and handling the disputes and negotiations that need a person.
reach: Bookkeeper AR work: cash application, reminder runs, master data
FP&A cash-in forecast and DSO input
Controller's bad-debt provision and credit insurer reporting
Credit checks and credit limits for new customers with sales
role.ceiling_note: About 930 of the role's ~1,600 hours are in these tasks; 45-55% can be freed. The limit is phone negotiation, judgement on disputes, legal steps and data quality in AFAS (KvK numbers, proof of delivery outside the listed systems).
skills_to_grow: Designing and tuning rules in AFAS and a credit management tool
AVG-aware data handling with third parties
role.ambitious_version: Run order-to-cash credit end to end: credit limits at onboarding, risk monitoring on every customer, same-day cash application, and a dispute feedback loop that cuts billing errors at the source, bringing DSO down and making the cash forecast reliable for month close.
